lesson_title: Whole Crates Only: Simplifying Algebraic Fractions
hook_text: That x² you just cancelled? It cost you every mark. Here's the storeroom rule.
clip_script: Walk into the shop's storeroom. Eight crates of cooldrink on the left, twelve on the right. Eight over twelve — and because both piles are built purely of identical crates, divide both by four: two over three. Nothing lost. Now change one detail. The left pile is eight crates PLUS one loose bottle. May you still divide crates out of both piles? No — the loose bottle belongs to no crate. That loose bottle is a plus sign. Cancel only what the whole top and the whole bottom are built from. Factorising is the repacking job: x squared minus twenty-five packs into x minus five, times x plus five. The bottom packs into x plus three, times x plus five. Both piles hold an x plus five crate — out it comes, whole, leaving x minus five over x plus three. And check like a shopkeeper: at x equal to one, both give minus one. Till balanced.
visual_style: A tidy storeroom: crate stacks forming a giant fraction, one loose bottle pulsing red beside its plus sign, sealed crates lifting away in pairs as brackets cancel, a till slip printing −1 = −1.
pacing: Easy counter-talk on the crates, hard stop at the loose bottle, smooth roll through the repack, crisp till-check ending.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and never cancel a term again.
